rationales.A: The sign beside the door lists exactly that: no oppressive taxes, no military kings, no compulsory military service, no knouts or dungeons.
rationales.B: The sign lists freedoms, not land. It promises no farm to any family.
rationales.C: No jobs are promised in the sign. The cartoon advertises liberty, not employment.
rationales.D: Background: that is the opposite of this welcome. The Chinese Exclusion Act came in 1882, two years after this cartoon.
rationales.general:
Read the sign on the door — the cartoonist put the whole argument there.
1. Look at the door. Uncle Sam welcomes a crowd of many origins into the 'U.S. Ark Refuge.'
2. Read the sign. No oppressive taxes, no military kings, no compulsory military service, no knouts or dungeons.
3. Name the attraction. Freedom from oppression, heavy taxes, and forced military service.
Remember: when a cartoon prints a list, the list is the answer — read it word for word.

source: original; stimulus viewed before writing — Joseph Keppler, Puck, 1880, public domain.
stem: What does the cartoon present as America's main attraction for immigrants?

stimulus.source_note: Joseph Keppler, 'Welcome to All!,' Puck magazine, 1880. Public domain. Library of Congress, LCCN2002719044. Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Welcome_to_all!_LCCN2002719044.jpg
stimulus.text: The cartoon shows Uncle Sam standing in the doorway of a building marked 'U.S. Ark Refuge,' welcoming a crowd of immigrants of many origins as they walk up the gangplank. A sign beside the door reads: 'No oppressive taxes, No military kings, No compulsory military service, No knouts or dungeons.' The caption reads 'Welcome to All!'
